subject.title: [Feature]: Self-hosted STT/TTS provider support in webchat (Route webchat TTS through the gateway instead of browser Speech API)

question: Should WebChat provider-backed voice be split into Gateway read-aloud first and editable batch push-to-talk STT through tools.media.audio, with browser/realtime Talk paths kept as distinct explicit modes?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but STT changes microphone UX, fallback behavior, private endpoint handling, and whether WebChat voice is batch dictation, realtime Talk, or both.

options.title: Split TTS and batch STT
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, review or replace the Gateway read-aloud PR for TTS, and let the editable dictation issue/PR own the batch STT product surface.

options.title: Narrow this issue to TTS
options.body: Retitle or close out the STT portion into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98026 and use this issue only for provider-backed read-aloud.

options.title: Pause for unified voice design
options.body: Defer both slices until maintainers define one WebChat voice model across Talk, dictation, TTS settings, and fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Split TTS and batch STT
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, review or replace the Gateway read-aloud PR for TTS, and let the editable dictation issue/PR own the batch STT product surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The open read-aloud candidate and related WebChat voice history make steipete the clearest available owner for the split-versus-unified product decision.
